coaching_qa.query: How do I bias the long head of the triceps on cable extensions?

coaching_qa.query: Explain how mechanical tension drives muscle growth without using fluff.
coaching_qa.generated_output:
Mechanical tension is the primary driver of hypertrophy. It occurs when a muscle generates force against a resistance while being stretched and shortened under load.

High-threshold motor units are recruited only under sufficient tension. When you lift a heavy weight with controlled tempo and a full range of motion, those fibers experience strain. This strain triggers mechanotransduction—a cellular signaling cascade that activates mTOR and other growth pathways.

The key variables are load, time under tension, and stretch. Lengthened partials or stretch-mediated pauses increase tension on individual sarcomeres, maximizing the signal for growth without relying on metabolic stress or pump.
